A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with readable main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained content matches after accounting for the added algorithm, appendix relabeling, code link, and pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward and constraint learning curves and runtime measurements across four environments in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and measurements in Section 5 and Appendix E. Its new actor-critic algorithm has no additional empirical results.

M1.justification: v2 adds Algorithm 5, Robust Constrained Actor-Critic (RCAC), alongside the unchanged RNPG/RPPG algorithms. It introduces separate learned reward and constraint critics, sampled transition batches, temporal-difference advantages, weight-norm perturbation corrections, and actor/critic losses. This is a substantive additional training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Constrained River-swim, Garnet(15,20), Modified Frozen-lake, and Garbage collection. The new RCAC pseudocode is not accompanied by an evaluated environment or additional task coverage.

E2.justification: RPPG and EPIRC-PGS remain the evaluated comparators in the corresponding benchmark experiments. RCAC does not participate in any reported comparison.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain the same data generation, discount factors, iteration budgets, learning rates, and lambda settings. Algorithm 5's symbolic training inputs do not document a new or revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The lambda sensitivity analysis in Figure 4 and the KL-versus-L2 regularization comparisons are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis of RCAC is added.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 11 retain the same description of runtime averages over multiple runs. Neither version adds or changes run counts, seed information, uncertainty reporting, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and plotted results in Figures 1–7 are unchanged. For example, Table 11 retains RNPG runtimes of 48.574 seconds for CRS and 78.406 seconds for Garnet. No RCAC outcomes are reported.

T1.justification: The existing definitions, assumptions, Proposition 1, Theorems 4.1 and 6.1, and appendix proofs and derivations are retained. RCAC introduces algorithmic update formulas without an accompanying theoretical derivation or guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about feasibility, iteration complexity, avoiding binary search, and computational efficiency. RCAC is not incorporated into the main contribution claims.

C2.justification: The result interpretations and Section 6 limitations, including finite state spaces and Assumption 2, remain unchanged. The CRPO discussion is retained under Appendix H instead of G; the RCAC addition supplies no substantive explanatory discussion.

D1.justification: The Section 5 implementation pointer changes from VocenInquisitor/RNPG to Sourav1429/RCAC_NPG. Algorithm 5 also supplies buffer construction and training-update details, although it gives no concrete network architecture or numerical hyperparameter configuration.

R1.justification: The same 55 references and related-work discussion are retained. The positioning relative to EPIRC-PGS and CRPO is unchanged, including the relabeled CRPO appendix.

P1.justification: v2 adds Appendix G, titled 'escalating to higher space', relabels the CRPO appendix as H, and updates the contents. Existing narrative text is otherwise unchanged apart from the implementation pointer and version stamp.

P2.justification: v2 adds the Algorithm 5 display on page 30, between portions of the CRPO discussion, and pushes its final lines onto page 31. Existing figures and tables retain their content and presentation; the layout changes are localized.

improvement.justification: Algorithm 5 adds potentially useful actor-critic training guidance, but its norm-based robustness correction and relationship to RNPG's guarantees are unexplained and receive no theoretical or empirical validation. The original evidence and finite-state limitation remain unchanged, while the new display interrupts the CRPO discussion. These potential benefits and clarity costs leave the net quality effect uncertain.
